svg.title: ECS + ALB — who points to whom
svg.text: Who points to whom — the configuration that links them
Each arrow is a reference I set in config. Example values are the agent lane; the WebUI and MCP services are wired exactly the same way.
added by ECS, not by me
① The service points at the target group
The target group is the meeting point — neither side references the other directly.
The listener rule says “send /acp* to agent-tg”. The service says “put my tasks into agent-tg”. Deploy a new revision or scale to 3 tasks and the ALB
needs no edit: ECS rewrites the target list, and the ALB just forwards to whatever healthy targets are listed.

text.tspan: Fargate tasks use awsvpc networking: each task gets its own network interface and private IP, and there is no EC2 instance to register — so a target is IP:port.

svg.text: * A forward action can also split traffic across several weighted target groups (e.g. blue/green deployments). Mine use one each.
